newsitem.title: UK: Cable & Wireless posts strong half-year profits.
newsitem.headline: Cable & Wireless posts strong half-year profits.

text.p: British telecommunications company Cable & Wireless Plc said Wednesday its underlying profits rose 9 percent in the first half of the year.
C&W said first-half pretax profits, excluding exceptional items, rose to 673 million pounds ($1.13 billion) -- above top analyst estimates of 668 million pounds ($1.12 billion).

The company, which recently concluded a major alliance with British cable operators, said revenues, including the firm's share in associates, rose 14 percent to 3.40 billion pounds ($5.7 billion), while group operating margins increased to 25 percent from 23 percent.
Chief Executive Richard Brown confirmed in an interview that Cable & Wireless had talked with NYNEX Corp., the New York-based regional phone company, and other firms about possible new alliances.
"I would characterise them as good business discussions," he said of the talks. "Where other companies have brought us opportunities to look at, we are responding to those ideas."
However, he emphasised the company felt no need to align itself with one partner.
C&W's plan to merge its Mercury unit with three British cable operators, including NYNEX CableComms Group, fuelled rumours it might seek to expand its alliance with NYNEX.
He declined to identify the other companies.
